title: Patchlet assembler and replayable checkpoint for admin repairs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On-call engineers frequently apply small one-off fixes encoded as ad-hoc scripts; these are hard to review, replay, and audit. We need a structured way to compose, validate, and replay small idempotent repair steps ("patchlets") into checkpointed remediation runs that are safe, observable, and recoverable.

Goal: Build a Patchlet Assembler service and a Replayable Checkpoint mechanism that lets support engineers: 1) assemble a sequence of patchlets into a checkpointed run, 2) perform a dry-run against a sandbox, 3) capture telemetry and snapshots at each checkpoint, and 4) replay or roll back the run safely in production with approval gates.

Scope: Implement registry-backed patchlet metadata (inputs, permissions, idempotency hints), a lightweight composer UI in the Admin Console (composer + checkpoint timeline), automated snapshotting of resource state before/after each checkpoint, integration with existing admin-sandbox for dry-runs, and a replay API that supports deterministic re-execution and partial rollbacks.

Design notes and constraints: Patchlets are small, single-purpose primitives (bash snippets, k8s manifests, API calls) packaged with metadata and a validation harness. Each patchlet must declare required permissions and an estimated blast radius. Checkpoint snapshots will use our existing runbook snapshot format (avoid introducing a new binary blob) and store pointers to immutable artifacts (logs, telemetry IDs, artifact SHA). Replay must be idempotent or detect non-determinism and surface a human review. Approval flow will integrate with the RBAC/approvals service; sensitive patchlets (high blast radius) require explicit two-person approval.

Success criteria: 1) First stable rollout enabling 10% of on-call fixes to be executed via patchlets (tracked by a patchlet usage metric), 2) MTTR for incidents using patchlets decreases by 20% in the first month, 3) Zero unauthorized production modifications (tracked by audit log coverage), and 4) Dry-run fidelity >= 90% (measured by divergence rate between sandbox and production dry-runs).

Rollout plan: Phase A (internal alpha) – implement registry + CLI composer + replay API + telemetry hooks; limited to SRE and one support pod. Phase B (beta) – add Console composer UI, sandbox dry-run integration, approval gating, and expanded telemetry; release to all on-call. Phase C (GA) – harden performance, retention policy for snapshots, compliance review, and docs/training.

Risks & mitigations: Non-deterministic effects (mitigate by validation harness and snapshot diffs); secret leakage in patchlets (mitigate by requiring secrets via KMS references, not inline); accidental mass remediation (require blast-radius limits and approval gates).

Artifacts: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/ops/patchlet-assembler, Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/4278, Sandbox harness dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/sandbox/patchlet-alpha
